post.caption:
Norman Borlaug bred dwarf wheat that put its energy into grain instead of stalk, so it would not collapse under heavy heads when fertilised. India adopted it and moved from famine risk in the 1960s to grain surplus within a decade. The honest version includes the costs: heavy fertiliser and water demand, groundwater depletion, and sharply reduced crop diversity. He did not end hunger. He bought time.
